validity.researcher_notes: The row records a 'Tyonek Gas Pipeline,' Nikiski->Beluga, 50.71 mi, 10-and-16-inch, StartYear1=1968, status=operating. No source found -- Alaska DNR's full State Pipeline Coordinator's ROW registry, the RCA, PHMSA/NPMS, EIA's pipeline-projects dataset (28 releases, zero 'Tyonek' matches), or the sheet's own harvested wiki-citation pool (5 citations: NPMS homepage, the RCA newsitem later found unrelated on Wayback, the ConocoPhillips timeline, and the DNR Tyonek W10 page already used above) -- documents a single system matching this exact profile under this name. The ONLY DNR-registered entity actually named 'Tyonek' is 'Tyonek W 10 Gas Pipeline': 7.5 mi, 10.75in OD, Tyonek Platform->Ladd Landing/BPL Junction connection, ROW effective 2018-04-26 -- a real, active, but much smaller and newer segment than recorded here, part of a documented family of short 'Tyonek Transportation System' legs (DNR's naming convention; a 2017 industry presentation on Harvest Alaska's Cook Inlet gas-gathering system separately corroborates this family of short segments around the Tyonek Platform, though that URL could not be re-located this session after the web-search tool budget was exhausted -- not cited as a ref for that reason). The one DNR entity whose length (52.50 mi, Nikiski start) is close to this row's 50.71 mi is the unrelated 'Nikiski Alaska Pipeline' -- a REFINED-PRODUCTS (jet fuel/gasoline/diesel) line to Anchorage, built 1976, not a gas line and not to Beluga; ruled out on commodity and terminus grounds, but flagged in case this row's length was mistakenly cross-referenced from an oil-side record. Existence cannot be confirmed as recorded; it may be (a) a real but differently-named/scoped system not yet matched to a DNR record, (b) a composite/ mislabeled duplicate of one or more of P7453 'Kenai Nikiski Pipeline' (no DNR entity by that name found either) and P7455 (see duplicate concern below), or (c) a legacy/GEM-only entry. Recommend a human check of RCA tariff filings and FERC-era state records specifically for a 1968 Cook Inlet gas line before further sourcing.

validity.recommendation: Adjudicate P7461 against P7455 (Cook Inlet Gas Gathering System / CIGGS Pipeline) -- same general Nikiski<->Tyonek/Beluga side-of-Cook-Inlet corridor. If they are the same physical system, note that DNR records CIGGS as CONVERTED TO OIL in 2018, which would make this row's Fuel='Gas'/Status='operating' (as a gas line) wrong going forward, not merely a naming duplicate.
validity.researcher_notes: DNR's 'CIGGS Pipeline' page describes CIGGS A (16in, 21 mi, tide/submerged lands across Cook Inlet) + CIGGS LP (10in, 4.7 mi, Middle Ground Shoals->Swanson River Oil Pipeline tie-in), built 1972, originally natural gas -- i.e. a 10-inch/16-inch pair, which is suggestively close to this row's recorded Diameter '10, 16'. DNR states: 'In 2018, the system was converted to transport oil as part of the CIPL Cross Inlet Pipeline Extension Project which re-routes oil from the west side of Cook Inlet to the Andeavor (Tesoro) Refinery in Nikiski' -- i.e. CIGGS now runs west-side-Cook-Inlet -> Nikiski, the same directionality as this row's Beluga-side-to-Nikiski endpoints (Beluga sits on the west side near Tyonek). This row's own routes-repo geometry (P7461.geojson, 1 feature/23 points) runs from near Tyonek/Beluga to Nikiski, consistent with that corridor (route geometry is background observation only, not a citable origin). CIGGS's combined system length (26.00 mi per DNR) does not match this row's 50.71 mi, so if P7461=CIGGS the length is materially wrong, or P7461 is a composite of CIGGS plus another segment. No DNR entity named 'Kenai Nikiski Pipeline' (P7453's name) was found in the full ROW registry either, so that duplicate hypothesis could not be evaluated this session. Not resolved -- flagged for cross-row adjudication, not merged unilaterally.
